cells.tense: There is a pull in you that has already gone and built something, and it is still pulling.
cells.act: choose which star to steer by and steer
cells.ask: Spend ten minutes naming the wants the work grew out of, then make the next move from the strongest of them.
cells.core:
You can see what a want has already made, and the pull keeps working while you see it. The shine comes off the work, not off you — trusting that is what lets yesterday add to today instead of starting over. Plenty of people can say what they hope for. Not many have the object in hand that hoping led to.

So take something you have made and mean to keep. Spend ten minutes naming the wants it grew out of, then make the next move inside the strongest of them. A page is not a testament; it gathers the pull into one aim. If the aim is private, keep it private — the ones who benefit from the work will feel it when the next thing lands.

cells.place: On the stretch of a calling where the want itself is what is drawn

cells.tense: You are already living on the far side of the making before anything has actually been made, and it is heavy to stand in.
cells.act: describe what is in front of your eyes in five plain lines, no conclusions
cells.ask: Look at the work in progress for a minute. Write five plain lines about what is actually here — finished, unfinished — and take the next step from them.
cells.core:
Where a pull drew you, it is carrying you past today into the ending. You talk about the thing as if it were done, measure the present against a settled result, and the finished part stops being a place to stand. The pull is real. Held this way it drops the ground it needs before the work is there to hold it up.

Stop and look at what is on the table for a minute. Five plain lines: what is finished, what is not, what is in your hands right now. Then take the next step from those lines rather than from where the whole thing is headed. Seeing where the work actually stands does not turn it down; it puts your feet back under it, and the want lands on what is here.

cells.tense: You are still standing at the moment the want first showed itself, and what exists now was your hands answering it.
cells.ask: Set aside fifteen minutes with empty hands and nothing to make better. Let whatever shows up show up. When the time is up, nothing needs reporting.
cells.core:
A want pulled; you followed it, and something exists because of that following. What you hold up as the account of it now is doubt that it arrived at all, and the making goes on with no wish in it. The work and the wishing have come apart. What ran out is the appetite, not the hands.

Set aside fifteen minutes with empty hands and nothing to make better. Let whatever shows up show up; decide nothing, fix nothing, and report nothing afterward. A direction gets seen again before anyone steers by it. Appetite comes back at a pace of its own, and something in you opens to meet it when it does.

cells.tense: The pull is doing the steering through your hands, and you tell it as if the work simply carried itself.
cells.act: meet someone in the middle and go on together
cells.ask: Pick one person who would care how the thing began. Tell them what you hoped it would become, then ask what they would want from it.
cells.core:
You look at what the pull produced and talk about the task as if it had planned itself. The want that chose the route you took stays at the edge of your account, and what you owe the work is taken up as duty instead of spoken. The record reads a chore. Something else is steering, and anyone looking at the work can tell the difference.

Let one person in on what you hoped the work would become — what it could still become — and ask what they would want from it. Hold that wish at the size it actually is instead of filing it under obligation. Saying it aloud brings it back where it belongs: not a thing you owe, a thing you chose.
cells.sheetLine: A wish chose the way you took, and you file it as a task.

attempts.check: Unsupported claim: that the person's practice already has a direction other people can see — the record gives the seat (aspiration present) but not evidence of visibility, so I keep the ask self-contained: looking at what the practice made says nothing about who else has noticed. The reader could reasonably say the Too Little cell narrows a real emptied-out stretch into one room of life; that is deliberate, since the record supports only where this capacity sits, not what happened. The asks survive a wrong read because each is one examinable act rather than a verdict — you can do the reflecting or the looking and still learn nothing about the diagnosis and something about the work. The sentence that serves the writer more than the person would be any line about what the completion wants from them; it is cut.
